description: What the model catalog suite must notice: the resolver loses its exactness, stops clamping a context window, guesses between makers, ignores the endpoint, forgets that a local runtime is local, spells one model two ways, offers a level the Hub has no setting for, or reads a snapshot of another format.

mutations.name: M1
mutations.what: an id that is in the catalog as written is no longer reported as exact

patches.old: if (Object.hasOwn(providers[providerId], id)) return answer(providerId, id, providers[providerId][id], 'exact');

mutations.name: M2
mutations.what: a context window above the bound the Hub accepts is passed on as it is

mutations.name: M3
mutations.what: an unknown endpoint and an id that two makers list is answered by the first maker (a guess)

mutations.name: M4
mutations.what: the endpoint no longer says which provider a custom connection is

mutations.name: M5
mutations.what: a local runtime is looked up in the catalog like any other endpoint

mutations.name: M6
mutations.what: dots are no longer written as dashes, so "4.5" and "4-5" are two models

mutations.name: M7
mutations.what: a level the Hub has no setting for ("default") is offered

mutations.name: M8
mutations.what: a snapshot of another format is read as version 1

mutations.name: M9
mutations.what: a gateway's spelling of another maker's model is no longer found through the canonical id
